messages:
Anita (People Ops): morning — quick heads up: Miguel's start moved to May 3 and he's switching to the NY office. Need to confirm work auth docs + whether an H‑1B amendment or other filings are required. @Theresa - Legal, can you advise?
Miguel (New Hire): I updated my home address on the employer portal yesterday. My EAD card is valid thru Oct 2026 and I have an SSN. Do I need to come onsite for the I‑9 or can we do remote verification?
Theresa - Legal: short answer: depends. Personal address change -> MIGUEL should file AR‑11 (USCIS) within 10 days: https://www.uscis.gov/ar-11. Worksite change to a different area of employment may trigger an H‑1B amendment/LCA. Please DM me the NY site address & whether duties change.
Anita (People Ops): we can do remote I‑9 via our vendor for the first pay period. Please upload original docs to ADP and complete the I‑9 section in Workday. Vendor link: https://verify.example.com (if vendor flags, you'll need to present originals to HR in-person).
Miguel (New Hire): I'm fully remote until June 1. If I don't complete I‑9 before payday, will payroll be blocked?
Payroll: Payroll: please complete I‑9 + direct deposit by 2024‑04‑28 to avoid a pay hold. If it's late, payroll may issue a delayed/partial payment while we hold tax docs.
ImmigrationBot: [Checklist] Required uploads: EAD front/back, SSN card, passport biographical page + visa page (if any), most recent I‑94. Action items: 1) File AR‑11 (personal address); 2) Submit worksite address to Legal for LCA review; 3) Complete I‑9 in Workday.
Ken (Eng): do we need to trigger a new LCA if the site is NY vs SF? Miguel will be onsite ~30% and remote 70%.
Theresa - Legal: LCA required when worksite falls outside the geographic area of the original LCA's prevailing wage area. 30% onsite still counts as worksite. I'll check the original LCA footprint — Ken, please DM the exact client/site address and expected weekly onsite days.
Anita (People Ops): Miguel, I'll schedule a 20m 1:1 to walk through I‑9, benefits enrollment, and how to request an employment verification letter for your spouse (if needed for stamping). Benefits eligibility might shift with the new start date; bring dependent docs if enrolling dependents.
Miguel (New Hire): thanks. Quick Q: spouse is on F‑2 — does she get an EAD? Also, can HR provide a letter for consulate?
Theresa - Legal: F‑2 dependents are not work‑authorized. If spouse needs work auth, that's a separate path (EAD under certain categories). We don't book consulate appointments, but HR can provide an employment verification letter. Anita will prepare it — allow 3 business days.
Anita (People Ops): snippet I'll use for the letter: ```To whom it may concern: Redwood Inference confirms employment for Miguel, start date May 3, position: SWE II, salary: $XXX. Contact people-ops@redwood.com for verification.``` Please DM any edits.
Miguel (New Hire): perfect — appreciate it :slightly_smiling_face:
Theresa - Legal: if amendment needed, timeline: LCA 7–10 business days typically, H‑1B amendment filing 5–15 business days to prepare (agency backlog varies). Premium processing optional (~15 calendar day adjudication once filed) — we'll quote cost if needed.
Theresa - Legal: estimated fees (ballpark): LCA legal/filing ~$800–1,200; amendment filing + legal ~$1,200–2,000; premium processing add ~$2,500. We'll confirm exacts after scope.
Ken (Eng): thanks — will provision budget if amendment is required.
Anita (People Ops): action items: Miguel: file AR‑11 & upload EAD/SSN to ADP; Miguel & Ken: DM Theresa the site address; Payroll: hold if I‑9 incomplete past cutoff; Anita: prepare verification letter + book 1:1.
Miguel (New Hire): filing AR‑11 now — will post confirmation link when done.
Anita (People Ops): great — ping this thread after you file. I'll mark this thread resolved once LCA review complete. Thanks everyone!
